Routing outcomes recorded:

- REQ-2400: Large claim, south region, requester says client asked twice → **B (priority desk) accepted**.
- REQ-2408: Small shipment, north region, “second attempt, first form bounced” → **C (regional office) accepted**.
- **C is not generally valid**: rejected for large refunds (south/east), small claims (north), large claim (south), and shipments from east. Do not select C solely because a request mentions a regional office.
- Repeated “client has been asking twice” and “second attempt” notes do not by themselves determine the route; identical/similar notes had both accepted and rejected outcomes.
- No evidence yet for A or D.
- Before choosing, prioritize the combination of request type, size, region, and context; current data is insufficient to infer a complete routing rule.

Routing outcomes recorded:

- REQ-2400: Large claim, south region, requester says client asked twice → **B (priority desk) accepted**.
- REQ-2408: Small shipment, north region, “second attempt, first form bounced” → **C (regional office) accepted**.
- REQ-2410: Small claim, east region, “same as last month” → **A (standard queue) accepted**.
- REQ-2411: Large invoice, north region, “no rush” → **A rejected**.
- REQ-2412: Large shipment, north region, “second attempt” → **B rejected**.
- REQ-2413/2415: Large claim, east region, “came through regional office” → **B rejected**.
- REQ-2414: Large invoice, east region, client asked twice → **B rejected**.
- REQ-2416: Large shipment, south region, “no rush” → **A accepted**.
- REQ-2417: Small shipment, east region, “same as last month” → **A rejected**.
- REQ-2418: Small claim, south region, “nothing missing” → **A accepted**.
- REQ-2419: Small shipment, south region, “second attempt” → **A accepted**.

Guidance:
- **A** is supported for small claims in east/south, large shipments in south, and small shipments in south, but is not valid for the tested small shipment/east or large invoice/north cases.
- **B** is supported only by the large claim/south example; it was rejected for large claims/invoices east and large shipment north.
- **C** is not generally valid: although accepted for one small shipment/north case, it has been rejected in multiple other contexts. Do not select it merely because a regional office is mentioned.
- Repeated-attempt, client-follow-up, “no rush,” and regional-office wording do not determine routing by themselves.
- **D has no evidence yet.** Use request type, size, region, and context together; the complete rule remains uncertain.

Routing outcomes recorded:

- REQ-2408: small shipment, north, second attempt → C.

- REQ-2418: small claim, south, nothing missing → A.
- REQ-2419: small shipment, south, second attempt → A.

Rejected:
- A: large invoice/north; small shipment/east; small refund/east; small invoice/east.
- B: large shipment/north; large claims/east and south; large invoice/east; large claim/north.
- C: small claims/north; prior contexts including small shipment/north? (Note: REQ-2408 is accepted, so C is context-dependent.)
- D: large refund/north; large shipment/north; small invoice/east; small shipment/east.

Updated guidance:
- No option is reliably determined by wording such as “no rush,” repeated attempts, client follow-up, “same as last month,” missing-item language, or regional-office/requester wording.
- A has some support for small claims (east/south), large shipments/south, and small shipments/south, but fails on several north/east cases.
- B is not generally valid; even large claims/south are now contradicted by two rejections.
- C is not generally valid: accepted once for small shipment/north but rejected for small claim/north.
- D currently has no accepted examples and is rejected across tested north/east cases.
- The routing rule remains unresolved; use request type, size, region, and context together, and avoid extrapolating from any single accepted case.

Routing outcomes recorded:

New accepted:
- REQ-2445: large claim, south, scanned paperwork → A.
- REQ-2446: small shipment, east, urgency → B.
- REQ-2448: small invoice, south, scanned paperwork → A.
- REQ-2449: large invoice, south, scanned paperwork → A.

New rejected:
- A: small shipment/east; small shipment/south; large shipment/north.
- C: large shipment/east; large invoice/east (two cases).

Updated guidance:
- A has strong repeated support across claim, invoice, and shipment requests in the south, including large claims/invoices and small invoices. It remains unreliable in north/east cases; small shipment/east was rejected.
- B is now supported for a small shipment/east, despite earlier rejection of the same type/region; routing may depend on unobserved factors or context, so do not treat this as a fixed rule.
- C has no accepted examples and is rejected for several east/north cases, including large shipment/east and large invoice/east. Its previous acceptance remains limited to small shipment/north.
- D remains unsupported, with no accepted examples.
- Request wording (urgency, repeated requests, scanned paperwork, “regional office,” “no rush,” missing-item notes) is not reliably predictive: identical or similar wording has produced different outcomes.
- Continue using type, size, region, and context together. Avoid extrapolating from any single acceptance; the underlying rule remains unresolved.

Routing outcomes recorded:

Accepted:
- A: large claim/east (REQ-2450, REQ-2455); large claim/south and large invoice/south; large claim/south? Earlier acceptance exists, but REQ-2459 was rejected; small invoice/south; large claim/south.
- B: small shipment/east (one accepted case).
- C: small shipment/north (prior); small refund/north (REQ-2454).

Rejected:
- A: small claim/south (REQ-2452); large claim/north; large claim/south (REQ-2459); large invoice/east; small shipment/east and south; large shipment/north.
- B: large refund/east; small refund/east; prior conflicting small shipment/east case.
- C: large shipment/east; large invoice/east; large shipment/north.
- D: no accepted examples.

Guidance:
- A can succeed for large claims in east, but identical large claim/south cases conflict (accepted earlier, rejected in REQ-2459). Do not treat region/type alone as deterministic. A remains unreliable in many north/east and some south cases.
- B remains weakly supported: one accepted small shipment/east, while other similar small shipment/east and refund/east cases were rejected.
- C has limited support for small shipment/north and small refund/north; otherwise rejected in observed large east/north cases.
- D remains unsupported.
- Wording and requester notes (urgency, scanned paperwork, regional office, repeated attempts, etc.) are not reliably predictive; similar wording has produced different outcomes.
- Use type, size, region, and context together. The underlying routing rule remains unresolved; avoid extrapolating from any single acceptance.
